The proposed proof needed x and x+e to BOTH be density points of the same class; the palette is a far-field object, so the correlation is at distance ~1, not at scale h -> 0. Refuted concretely by the hexagonal colouring, where P_x(e) = {c0(x+e)} for a.e. x,e, so the centre colour can reappear in the palette. Do not re-attempt this in the 'self-containment' form.

The Steinhaus step 'a measurable set avoiding distance exactly 1 has measure zero' is FALSE: measurable unit-free sets can have positive measure and unbounded diameter (two far-apart small disks). Only connected unit-free sets have diameter <= 1 (the paper's section 7 fact). Do not use Steinhaus to bound colour classes.
